title: Minutes in meetings
prompt:
A calendar stores meetings as `[start, end]` pairs of whole minutes after midnight, with `start < end`. A meeting covers the time from `start` up to `end`, so `[60, 90]` lasts 30 minutes. Meetings can overlap, sit inside one another, touch end to start, and come in any order.

Write `busyMinutes(meetings)` that returns how many minutes are covered by at least one meeting. An empty calendar returns 0.

Examples:

- `busyMinutes([[60, 90]])` returns `30`
- `busyMinutes([[0, 30], [10, 40]])` returns `40` (the overlap counts once)
hints: If the meetings were sorted by start time, what would you need to remember as you walk through them?
When the next meeting starts before the current busy block ends, what happens to the block, and what if it starts after?
Have you handled a meeting that sits entirely inside the current block, so that the end of the block never moves backwards?
